name: Aether Industries Ltd
title: Aether Industries Ltd - 543534 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Aether FY26 consolidated revenue rose 38% to INR11,601 million and PAT 39% to INR2,195 million, while Q4 EBITDA fell to INR814 million from INR1,099 million in Q3.
summary.overview: FY26 delivered strong growth, with revenue up 38% YoY and EBITDA margin at 31%. Q4 was softer sequentially: revenue of INR3,051 million (vs INR3,188 million in Q3), EBITDA of INR814 million and PAT of INR540 million, hit by the absence of a one-time Q3 FLOP claim income, a INR70 million fire-related inventory provision and about INR10 million of year-end provisions. Management said LSM pricing rose over 20% YoY and 18% QoQ in Q4 and has held in April and May, though part of March LSM volume slipped into April and May due to logistics. Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin of 29-30% and PAT margin of about 19-20%, with Site 5 Phase 1 commercialisation and Site 3++ ramp-up as drivers.

segments.name: LSM (large-scale manufacturing)
segments.commentary: Contributed 43% of sales. Q4 LSM revenue was about INR111 crore vs INR131 crore in Q3, attributed to March shipments slipping into April-May; pricing up over 20% YoY in Q4.

segments.name: CRAMS and CEM combined
segments.commentary: Contributed 55% of revenue; CRAMS was about 10% of revenue in FY26 (INR107 crore in absolute terms vs INR100 crore prior year per management). Target of 70%+ of sales from CRAMS and CEM in the coming years, and by FY30.

segments.name: Site 4
segments.commentary: Revenue grew from INR50 crore to INR220 crore (4x), now 21% of total sales.

segments.name: Pharma plus agro
segments.commentary: Share at 46% of sales; material science at 17%, which management expects to grow with Site 3++ ramp-up.

segments.name: Baker Hughes
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue to Baker Hughes about INR76 crore (INR68 crore of material supplies, rest CRAMS); management reports no order cuts or delays.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 29-30% and PAT margin at 19-20%; no revenue growth guidance given.
Working capital cycle expected to fall to about 160 days by end FY27 (target 150 days) from 179 days.
Debt to rise by INR200-250 crore by end FY27 as capex is funded post QIP; increase to be sequential and gradual.
Capex FY27 guided at INR3,000-3,500 million, mainly Site 5 and new R&D site; total remaining capex about INR1,500-1,600 crore over next four years.
Site 5 Phase 1 expected to be commercialised fully in FY27; Site 5 asset turn target 1.5-1.75x.
Elevated LSM pricing expected to hold for next 2-3 quarters; exports expected to recover to 50-60% of top line.
Target product mix of 70% CRAMS and CEM and about 30% LSM within next 2-3 years (no firm timeline given).
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation: Site 2 at 75%, Site 3 at 70%, Site 4 at 55%.

Site 5: 4 production blocks constructed, 2 ready for water and solvent trials; 3 new LSM products (2 pharma, 1 agro) to be commissioned by end May or first week of June 2026; 16 production blocks planned on current site and about 4 more on adjoining 15-acre plot (46 acres total, ~20 blocks).
Interim R&D expansion completed: 2 new labs, 18 fume hoods (incl. 5 engineering), 400 MHz NMR; commercialisation from Q2 FY27.
New R&D site with 15 labs (incl. 5 engineering labs) and close to 140 fume hoods, expected commissioning in Q2 FY28.
Site 3++ commercialised in FY26 and ramping up; deliveries to Milliken began in April and May 2026.
demand_pricing: LSM pricing rose sharply after the conflict began and held through April and May 2026; management expects prices to stay elevated for 2-3 quarters.
No volume softness from customers so far, and no demand hoarding seen; Converge polyol demand reported as niche (CASE segment) with no disruption from Saudi Aramco JV supply.
Management says CEM contracts are open cost P&L, so raw material inflation is passed through; LSM may see temporary margin delta.
Exports fell as CEM customers routed sales via Indian subsidiaries; management expects exports to return to 50-60% of top line.
Semiconductor materials opportunity expected to triple by 2030; first phase of 400 tonnes of molecules at $40-50/kg.
Site 5 LSM products priced at $30-40/kg; competition from China and a Japanese manufacturer.

qa_highlights.question: Why did LSM revenue fall QoQ despite ~20% price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Kushal Doshi said March shipments were held up by logistics and were shipped in April-May at higher prices; no sign of volume softness yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Q4 margins lower than Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Faiz Nagariya cited the INR70 million fire-related inventory write-off, absence of the Q3 FLOP claim income and year-end provisions of about INR10 million; no underlying margin issue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 working capital and debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital days expected to fall to about 160 (target 150) by end FY27 from 179; debt to rise INR200-250 crore by end FY27, gradually.

qa_highlights.question: What is the remaining capex and asset turn?
qa_highlights.answer: Remaining capex about INR1,500-1,600 crore over four years, mainly Site 5 and new R&D site; Site 5 asset turn targeted at 1.5-1.75x.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue guidance for FY27 and growth drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: No revenue growth guidance; Site 4, Site 3++, the new R&D fume hoods and Site 5 Phase 1 are named drivers; site-wise numbers not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any Baker Hughes impact from the conflict?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 Baker Hughes revenue about INR76 crore (INR68 crore supplies); continuous orders with no delays or cancellations.

risks_watch: Q4 margin dip partly tied to one-offs; management says Q1 FY27 should recover, so confirm in next results.
Sustainability of LSM price increases once the Middle East disruption normalises; management expects 2-3 quarters of elevated pricing.
Working capital at 179 days remains high; target 160 days by FY27 depends on Site 3++ and Site 5 ramp and debtor collection.
Site 5 commissioning timelines (end May / early June 2026) and whether commercial volumes start in Q1 FY27.
Rising debt to fund capex, with cost of debt not disclosed.
Fire safety: second fire incident at an external warehouse near Site 1 (March 11, 2026); Site 2 fire insurance claim expected to settle by end Q1 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on pricing and the Site 5 and R&D pipeline, with management stating the new growth phase is underway. More cautious and non-committal on guidance: no revenue growth figure, no timeline for the 70:30 mix, and no site-wise or cost-of-debt detail.
key_quotes: Pricing has been exceptionally strong over 20% year-on-year and 18% quarter-on-quarter in Q4.
Validation batches are done and orders are already in hand.
We believe this pricing environment is sustainable in the medium term.
